zh: 大家能听清我说话吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: All levels coming through good?
zh: 音量都正常吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: All right.
zh: 好的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Sweet.
zh: 太好了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, how's everyone doing?
zh: 那么，大家最近怎么样？

speaker: Unknown
en: How's everyone doing?
zh: 大家过得如何？

speaker: Unknown
en: Better?
zh: 好点了吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: OK, there we go.
zh: 好，就是这样。

speaker: Unknown
en: Cool.
zh: 很好。

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, I hope the conference has been good for everybody.
zh: 我希望这次大会对大家来说都收获满满。

speaker: Unknown
en: I appreciate you all being here to listen to a chat from me.
zh: 感谢各位来到这里听我的分享。

speaker: Unknown
en: For anyone who hasn't met me at the booth yet, my name is Matt Lawler.
zh: 对于还没在展台见过我的朋友，我叫 Matt Lawler。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm a Forward Deployed Engineer at Assembly AI, mostly focused on bringing in inbound customers, helping win their business, making sure that they have a good time building with our API.
zh: 我是 Assembly AI 的一名前置部署工程师(Forward Deployed Engineer),主要负责引入入站客户、帮他们达成合作，并确保他们在使用我们 API 构建的过程中有良好的体验。

speaker: Unknown
en: So how many other Forward Deployed Engineers are out in the audience right now?
zh: 那么在座的各位有多少也是前置部署工程师？

speaker: Unknown
en: Any of us?
zh: 有吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: OK, couple.
zh: 好，有几位。

speaker: Unknown
en: Cool.
zh: 很好。

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, still coming through OK?
zh: 好，音频还能正常听到吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: All right.
zh: 好的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, so I wanted to make sure I gave you guys an overview of some of the go-to-market engineering stuff that we've been doing at Assembly AI that maybe you can apply to your own FTE team, or maybe you can apply to your company as something that you can do as an easy win for your customers.
zh: 是这样的，我想给大家介绍一下我们在 Assembly AI 做的一些市场工程(go-to-market engineering)方面的工作，也许你们可以应用到自己前置部署工程师(FDE)团队中，或者作为一项能轻松为客户带来的速赢举措应用到你们公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: So for a little bit of overview of Assembly AI, in case you haven't heard of us, we provide voice AI infrastructure.
zh: 先简单介绍一下 Assembly AI,以防有人没听说过我们：我们提供语音 AI 基础设施。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we train our own foundation models for speech-to-text primarily, but we're starting to branch into other parts of the voice agent space.
zh: 我们主要训练自己的语音转文本(speech-to-text)基础模型，但我们也开始向语音智能体领域的其他方向拓展。

speaker: Unknown
en: So if anyone's ever had a Fireflies note-taker join your meeting or something like that, you've already seen a transcript from Assembly AI.
zh: 如果有人的会议中加入过 Fireflies 之类的会议记录员，那你其实已经见过 Assembly AI 的转写文本了。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we train our own foundational models, not only for async use cases like meeting recordings and things like that, but also for real-time voice agents.
zh: 我们训练自己的基础模型，不仅用于像会议录音这样的异步场景，也用于实时的语音智能体。

speaker: Unknown
en: So if you've ever used
zh: 所以如果你曾经用过

speaker: Unknown
en: Like a phone customer support agent when you called in somewhere and it wasn't a human, or like drive-through ordering, they're more than likely building with AssemblyAI's models.
zh: 比如你打电话给某处客服，接听的不是真人，而是电话客服智能体，或者是得来速点餐，它们大概率就是在用 AssemblyAI 的模型构建的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And for anyone who's building a voice agent, now you can use us for the entire stack, not just speech-to-text.
zh: 对于正在构建语音智能体的人来说，现在你们可以把整个技术栈都交给我们，而不仅仅是语音转文本。

speaker: Unknown
en: So you can use our voice agent API, and we'll string together the speech-to-text, the LLM, and the text-to-speech as well.
zh: 你可以使用我们的语音智能体 API,我们会把语音转文本、LLM 以及文本转语音(text-to-speech)串接起来。

speaker: Unknown
en: As our competitors know, as we know, as anyone in the voice AI space knows, demand is absolutely insane for voice AI right now.
zh: 正如我们的竞争对手知道的、我们自己知道的、语音 AI 领域所有人都知道的那样，现在语音 AI 的需求简直是疯狂。

speaker: Unknown
en: So Assembly, at our current moment, we see around 1,000 API signups every single day, which is somewhat of the theme of why we were focusing on automation and wanting to build kind of a new support bot for our team, because at least until like two days ago, I was the only onboarding engineer at Assembly AI.
zh: 所以 Assembly 目前的状况是，我们每天大约有 1,000 个 API 注册，这也是为什么我们聚焦于自动化、想为团队构建一个新支持机器人的原因之一，因为至少在两天之前，我还是 Assembly AI 唯一的入职引导工程师(onboarding engineer)。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so you can imagine, as much as I'd want to talk to 1,000 new signups every single day,
zh: 所以你可以想象，尽管我很想每天和 1,000 个新注册用户都聊一聊，

speaker: Unknown
en: It's just not feasible.
zh: 但这根本不可行。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we had to build something to solve that problem.
zh: 所以我们必须构建某种东西来解决这个问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then for anyone here who doesn't know what a Forward Deployed Engineer is, it's a very catch-all title.
zh: 对于在座还不知道什么是前置部署工程师的人来说，这是一个非常笼统的头衔。

speaker: Unknown
en: It varies a lot at every different company.
zh: 在每家公司的具体职责差异很大。

speaker: Unknown
en: But effectively, we want to get deployed with our end customers.
zh: 但本质上，我们要深入到终端客户那里去部署。

speaker: Unknown
en: We want to understand their use case.
zh: 我们要理解他们的使用场景。

speaker: Unknown
en: We want to make sure that we are building exactly what they need.
zh: 我们要确保我们构建的正是他们需要的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we frequently commit code directly to their repositories.
zh: 所以我们经常直接向他们的代码仓库提交代码。

speaker: Unknown
en: We usually meet with them several times a month, if not a week.
zh: 我们通常每月与他们见面好几次，有时甚至每周都有。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we really try to understand their use case and get to know them very personally.
zh: 我们真心试图理解他们的使用场景，并与他们建立非常个人的了解。

speaker: Unknown
en: So like at least on the inbound side, for anyone who comes into assembly who wants to build with us, we are the people that are their main point of contact for anything they need on the technical, commercial side, anything that they might need they get from us, their FDE.
zh: 至少在入站这边，任何来到 Assembly 想与我们合作构建的人，我们就是他们在技术和商务方面任何需求的主要联系人，他们需要的任何东西都从他们的 FDE 这里获得。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we're responsible for winning their business and building that trust with them.
zh: 我们负责赢得他们的业务，并与他们建立信任。

speaker: Unknown
en: So it's a great services model.
zh: 所以这是一个很棒的服务模式。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's great if we can actually get that kind of relationship with every customer.
zh: 如果我们能与每个客户都建立这样的关系，那当然很棒。

speaker: Unknown
en: But again, with 1,000 API signups every day, I can't be one to many serving that many customers and getting on that many calls.
zh: 但再说一次，每天 1,000 个 API 注册，我不可能以一对多的方式服务这么多客户、参加这么多通话。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so ultimately, this doesn't really scale super well.
zh: 所以归根结底，这种模式并不能很好地规模化。

speaker: Unknown
en: We want to make sure that we're freeing ourselves up to be leading human-led deals as much as possible, but we can't do that with every deal.
zh: 我们希望尽可能把自己解放出来，去主导由人主导的交易(human-led deals),但我们不可能在每一笔交易上都做到这一点。

speaker: Unknown
en: Not every customer win can be hand-built by us.
zh: 并不是每一个客户成功案例都能由我们手工打造。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we can't just continue to hire more and more FDEs if we're going to try and serve more and more customers.
zh: 而且如果我们想要服务越来越多的客户，就不能一直雇用越来越多的 FDE。

speaker: Unknown
en: So ultimately, for anyone who's an FTE in here, if you're looking to become an FTE, if you already have an FTE team at your company, I would encourage you to take that knowledge that you have as an FTE and try to automate yourself out of a job.
zh: 所以归根结底，对于在座的任何一位 FTE，如果你想成为一名 FTE，如果你的公司已经有了一个 FTE 团队，我鼓励你把你作为 FTE 所掌握的知识拿来，尝试把自己从这份工作中自动化出去。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think that should be your role every single day.
zh: 我认为这应该是你每一天的角色。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you want to serve your customers better, if you want to work with them more, and if you want to deliver a better customer experience at scale, you can't be the bottleneck to having a good customer experience.
zh: 如果你想更好地服务你的客户，如果你想与他们更多地合作，如果你想在规模化交付更好的客户体验，你就不能成为良好客户体验的瓶颈。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we learn that firsthand.
zh: 而这是我们亲身体会到的。

speaker: Unknown
en: So again, we were drowning in inbound volume.
zh: 再说一次，我们当时被涌入的量淹没了。

speaker: Unknown
en: You can see we basically had 1,000 API signups up there earlier.
zh: 你们可以看到，我们前面基本上有 1,000 个 API 注册。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we had the natural instinct that a lot of teams do, where we were like, we just need to deflect more conversations.
zh: 我们和很多团队一样有一种本能的反应，就是：我们只需要 deflect 掉更多的对话。

speaker: Unknown
en: I just want to talk to fewer people.
zh: 我只想和更少的人说话。

speaker: Unknown
en: I want to make sure I'm freeing myself up to work on more important stuff.
zh: 我想确保把自己解放出来，去做更重要的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we basically bought this off-the-shelf support bot.
zh: 所以我们基本上买了一个现成的支持机器人。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we're like, let's point it at the docs.
zh: 然后我们说，把它指向文档吧。

speaker: Unknown
en: It'll answer all the docs questions for us.
zh: 它会替我们回答所有文档相关的问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's going to be great.
zh: 一定会很棒。

speaker: Unknown
en: We'll never have to answer a simple question from customers again.
zh: 我们再也不用回答客户的简单问题了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it only resolved about 10% of the conversations.
zh: 结果它只解决了大约 10% 的对话。

speaker: Unknown
en: So it helped.
zh: 所以还是有帮助的。

speaker: Unknown
en: You can imagine if we had like 1,000 conversations a day, 100 of those were now entered by a bot.
zh: 你可以想象，如果我们一天有 1,000 个对话，其中 100 个现在由机器人接管了。

speaker: Unknown
en: But then our team still had to field 900 tickets a day.
zh: 但我们的团队每天仍然要处理 900 个工单。

speaker: Unknown
en: So it wasn't exactly very scalable.
zh: 所以这并不算很有可扩展性。

speaker: Unknown
en: So 10% end-to-end resolution rate wasn't good enough.
zh: 所以 10% 的端到端解决率是不够好的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And ultimately, we couldn't iterate fast enough to be able to fix this.
zh: 而且归根结底，我们没办法足够快地迭代来修复这个问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: We didn't have access to the system prompt.
zh: 我们拿不到 system prompt。

speaker: Unknown
en: We didn't have access to the tools.
zh: 我们拿不到工具。

speaker: Unknown
en: We didn't have access to the RAG infrastructure.
zh: 我们拿不到 RAG 基础设施。

speaker: Unknown
en: So anytime we needed to change something, we'd go to this vendor and they'd say, well, it's on the roadmap.
zh: 所以每次我们需要改点什么，我们去找这个供应商，他们会说，嗯，这个在路线图上。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that didn't quite work for us.
zh: 这对我们来说不太行得通。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we wanted to build our own.
zh: 所以我们想自己造一个。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we built another member of our team rather than hiring one, and we named him Joey.
zh: 于是我们「造」了另一个团队成员而不是去雇一个，我们给他起名叫 Joey。

speaker: Unknown
en: So anyone now who reaches out to us, whether it's on our chat widget on our site, whether you reach out to contact sales, whether you reach out to our support alias, you're going to meet Joey instead of a human.
zh: 所以现在任何联系我们的人，无论是通过我们网站上的聊天组件，无论是联系销售，还是发到我们的支持邮箱，你遇到的都会是 Joey 而不是人类。

speaker: Unknown
en: He's the first line of defense now for every single conversation that happens in bounded assembly, and he's built to be the most infinitely scalable FDE on our team.
zh: 他现在是 bounded assembly 里发生的每一个对话的第一道防线，而且他被打造为我们团队上可无限扩展的 FDE。

speaker: Unknown
en: So he remembers past conversations with you.
zh: 所以他记得与你过去的对话。

speaker: Unknown
en: We track all of his metrics via Pylon because he's still a member of our support team.
zh: 我们通过 Pylon 追踪他的所有指标，因为他仍然是我们支持团队的一员。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so he has access to Pylon to manage conversations and remember who you are.
zh: 所以他可以访问 Pylon 来管理对话，并记住你是谁。

speaker: Unknown
en: And he's built on top of the Claude Agent SDK.
zh: 而且他是构建在 Claude Agent SDK 之上的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so the cool things that he's able to do is he can manage his own infrastructure.
zh: 所以他能做的很酷的事情是，他可以管理自己的基础设施。

speaker: Unknown
en: He has a file system.
zh: 他有一个文件系统。

speaker: Unknown
en: He can write and debug code for you.
zh: 他可以为你编写和调试代码。

speaker: Unknown
en: He can call tools.
zh: 他可以调用工具。

speaker: Unknown
en: He can give himself new abilities.
zh: 他可以给自己赋予新能力。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so he's actually able to operate more like an FTE and less like just a standard chatbot that you'd be talking with on most major sites nowadays.
zh: 所以他实际上更像是作为一个 FTE 在运作，而不只是你现在在大多数主流网站上会聊到的那种标准聊天机器人。

speaker: Unknown
en: So if you want to know a little bit of how to build your own Joey, the architecture kind of has four major parts.
zh: 所以如果你想了解一点如何打造你自己的 Joey，这个架构大致有四个主要部分。

speaker: Unknown
en: So as everyone might know from working with Claude, Markdown is your friend.
zh: 正如每个用过 Claude 的人可能知道的，Markdown 是你的朋友。

speaker: Unknown
en: You should be giving Markdown files to Claude so that he understands everything about your business.
zh: 你应该把 Markdown 文件喂给 Claude，让他了解你业务的一切。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so we wanted him to have access to all of our documentation and be trained up on it all the time.
zh: 所以我们希望他能够访问我们所有的文档，并持续不断地在上面接受训练。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we checked all of our docs out as local markdown and gave it to Joey.
zh: 于是我们把所有文档以本地 markdown 的形式检出，交给了 Joey。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so any time that we push an update to our documentation system, he's able to get all of those files and he has them locally in his file system.
zh: 所以每当我们向文档系统推送更新时，他都能拿到所有这些文件，并本地保存在他的文件系统里。

speaker: Unknown
en: So actually what's really cool is if our entire doc site was down right now, you could go to Joey and still get live answers on all the newest stuff that we've shipped without our team having to actually get involved.
zh: 所以真正很酷的一点是，如果我们整个文档网站现在挂了，你也可以去找 Joey，仍然能得到关于我们最新发布内容的实时解答，而无需我们团队真正介入。

speaker: Unknown
en: For retrievals, we can give you a good answer.
zh: 对于检索，我们可以给你一个不错的答案。

speaker: Unknown
en: We partner with Voyage, so we use their embeddings so that he gets the most relevant documents up front so he doesn't have to spend a lot of time searching and he can get you a faster answer.
zh: 我们与 Voyage 合作，所以我们使用他们的嵌入，这样他就能一开始就拿到最相关的文档，从而不用花很多时间搜索，并且能更快地给你答案。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then since he has all these docs as local files, if he gets confused or he needs to string together multiple resources to create a response, he can agentically search the file system that he lives on so that he can go and find those resources for you.
zh: 然后，由于他把所有这些文档都存为本地文件，如果他感到困惑，或者需要把多个资源串联起来以生成回答，他可以以智能体方式搜索他所处的文件系统，从而为你找到那些资源。

speaker: Unknown
en: So you can kind of go into this deep thinking mode where he's able to search across all these resources.
zh: 所以你可以进入这种深度思考模式，他能够跨所有这些资源进行搜索。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then we shipped it on Railway.
zh: 然后我们把它部署在了 Railway 上。

speaker: Unknown
en: We didn't want to deal with infrastructure.
zh: 我们不想处理基础设施。

speaker: Unknown
en: We didn't want to spin up an EC2.
zh: 我们不想启动一台 EC2。

speaker: Unknown
en: We didn't want to have to change instance types.
zh: 我们不想去更换实例类型。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we deployed it all on Railway.
zh: 所以我们把它全部部署在了 Railway 上。

speaker: Unknown
en: Their service is pretty incredible.
zh: 他们的服务相当不可思议。

speaker: Unknown
en: Basically, we can just go ahead and see if he has a bad conversation with someone in Slack.
zh: 基本上，我们可以直接去看看他是否在 Slack 上和某人的对话很糟糕。

speaker: Unknown
en: We can write a PR real quick, and we can deploy it.
zh: 我们可以很快写一个 PR，然后部署。

speaker: Unknown
en: And within 30 seconds, there's a new live version of Joey.
zh: 30 秒内，就会有一个新的线上版 Joey。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we're able to iterate really, really quickly.
zh: 所以我们能够非常非常快速地迭代。

speaker: Unknown
en: We've actually had times where we've actually monitored a live conversation, caught a bug, deployed a fix, and then it's been proved for the rest of the session, and that customer doesn't even have to know that we shipped that fix behind the scenes.
zh: 实际上有几次，我们实时监控一场对话，发现了一个 bug，部署了修复，然后在会话的剩余时间里它就被验证有效了，而那个客户甚至不需要知道我们在幕后发布了那个修复。

speaker: Unknown
en: So Joey is able to basically get updated whenever we want, so we actually have full control over everything that he does.
zh: 所以 Joey 基本上可以在我们想要的任何时候得到更新，所以我们对他做的每件事都有完全的控制权。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so the results were pretty remarkable from us building this.
zh: 因此，我们构建这个东西的成果相当惊人。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it's another reason why I wanted to encourage everyone who's here to try and build your own Joey.
zh: 这也是为什么我想鼓励在座的每一位尝试构建你自己的 Joey 的另一个原因。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we went from 10% to 80% end-to-end resolution rate in just the first week of deploying this build with a pretty naive implementation.
zh: 所以，在部署这个构建的第一周内，我们就把端到端解决率从 10% 提升到了 80%，而且用的是相当朴素的实现。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we did that all for around $700 a month in both token and infrastructure costs.
zh: 而且我们总共只花了大约每月 700 美元的 token 和基础设施成本就做到了这一切。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we resolved 80% of our tickets end-to-end with no human in the loop.
zh: 所以我们在没有人工介入的情况下端到端解决了 80% 的工单。

speaker: Unknown
en: Some people like to game these metrics.
zh: 有些人喜欢在这些指标上做手脚。

speaker: Unknown
en: They'll say, like, oh, we resolved 80% but only on, like, a subset of types of tickets.
zh: 他们会说，比如，哦，我们解决了 80%，但只在某一类工单子集上。

speaker: Unknown
en: Not the case here.
zh: 这里不是这种情况。

speaker: Unknown
en: You cannot reach a human directly unless you go through Joey and you tell him to escalate.
zh: 除非你经过 Joey 并让他升级，否则你无法直接联系到人工。

speaker: Unknown
en: So he actually does handle 100% of these inbound tickets for us now.
zh: 所以他现在实际上为我们处理 100% 的这些入站工单。

speaker: Unknown
en: And he only escalates 20% of them to a human for the right reasons.
zh: 而且他只出于正确的理由把其中 20% 升级给人工。

speaker: Unknown
en: Maybe it's a rate change.
zh: 也许是费率变更。

speaker: Unknown
en: Maybe it's a data opt-out.
zh: 也许是数据退出。

speaker: Unknown
en: Maybe you need to sign an agreement with us.
zh: 也许你需要和我们签署一份协议。

speaker: Unknown
en: Needs that only an FTE or someone from legal needs to be involved in.
zh: 这些是只有全职员工或法务需要介入的需求。

speaker: Unknown
en: These are things that actually still need a human, but eventually we can automate.
